summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with infected breast ulcers and right heel pain. She had recently undergone a breast biopsy, and the wound became infected due to inadequate dressing changes. Cultures grew Pseudomonas, and she was treated with intravenous antibiotics, later transitioned to oral therapy. Imaging showed no abscess or osteomyelitis. Her right heel had a non-infected pressure injury with underlying bone spurs, managed with offloading. She also had symptomatic bladder sludge in the setting of low urine output from ESRD, treated with a short-term catheter and antibiotics. Social work coordinated home care with family support, avoiding rehab placement per patient preference. She remained stable throughout, completed dialysis, and was discharged home on a 14-day antibiotic course with follow-up arranged.
